**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examinations. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.

Sujet scanné de 2 pages (page de garde et six questions sur une page), lu en image ; aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées, au nombre exact d'éléments demandé ; d'autres réponses valables existent pour les questions de liste, et le barème d'un point par élément est une hypothèse (le sujet ne le détaille pas).

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = 25 marks » et les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour chacune des 6 questions (aucun écart). Quand une sous-question (a), (b), (c) ou (d) porte des parties (i) et (ii), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des parties imprimées.

Question 3(a) : le corrigé utilise les valeurs du programme (1 g de glucide ou de protéine = environ 17 kJ = 4 kcal ; 1 g de lipide = environ 37 kJ = 9 kcal) : 10 x 17 + 3 x 37 + 43 x 17 = 1 012 kJ, soit 239 kcal (recalculé avec Python). Certains manuels emploient 16 kJ pour les glucides et les protéines (959 kJ) ou 3,75 kcal pour les glucides ; la méthode est donnée et le corrigé signale la variante 16 kJ.

Question 3(b) : la ligne « Classify food nutrients and give example in each case. (4 marks) » est imprimée SANS lettre, juste sous 3(b), avant 3(c). Elle est transcrite comme seconde partie de 3(b), dont `points` = 5 + 4 = 9 ; la somme de la question reste 6 + 9 + 6 + 4 = 25. Le sujet n'impose pas de critère de classement : le corrigé donne un tableau par fonction (énergie, construction, protection) avec les six classes de nutriments.

Question 3(c)(ii) : l'usage de la table de composition des aliments est un fait de cours usuel ; aucune donnée chiffrée tirée d'une table n'est avancée. Question 3(d) : les facteurs de disponibilité des aliments sont des réponses modèles (d'autres sont valables).

questions.enonce_markdown:
If a cup of fruit flavoured yoghurt contains 10g of protein, 3g of fats and 43g of carbohydrates. Calculate the amount of energy provided by the yoghurt.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method.** Energy = (mass of each nutrient) x (energy value of 1 g of that nutrient), then add.

Energy values: 1 g of protein = 17 kJ, 1 g of fat = 37 kJ, 1 g of carbohydrate = 17 kJ (1 g of protein or carbohydrate is about 4 kcal and 1 g of fat about 9 kcal).

| Nutrient | Mass (g) | Energy per gram (kJ) | Energy (kJ) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Protein | 10 | 17 | $10 \times 17 = 170$ |
| Fat | 3 | 37 | $3 \times 37 = 111$ |
| Carbohydrate | 43 | 17 | $43 \times 17 = 731$ |
| **Total** | | | $170 + 111 + 731 = 1012$ |

**The yoghurt provides about 1012 kJ** (about 1.0 MJ).

In kilocalories: $10 \times 4 + 3 \times 9 + 43 \times 4 = 40 + 27 + 172 = 239$, that is **about 239 kcal**.

(If the value 16 kJ per gram is used for protein and carbohydrate instead of 17 kJ, the total is $160 + 111 + 688 = 959$ kJ; the method is the same.)
themes: energy from food and body metabolism

questions.enonce_markdown:
State five (5) functions of water in the body.

(5 marks)

Classify food nutrients and give example in each case.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**State five functions of water in the body (1 mark each).**

1. Water is a **solvent**: nutrients dissolve in it and chemical reactions of the cells take place in it.
2. It **transports** nutrients, oxygen, hormones and wastes in the blood.
3. It **regulates the body temperature**: sweat evaporates from the skin and cools the body.
4. It **helps digestion**: it is a part of saliva and of the other digestive juices, and it softens the food and the waste so that they pass easily (it prevents constipation).
5. It helps the body to **get rid of wastes** (urine and sweat) and it **lubricates** the joints and the mucous linings.

**Classification of food nutrients, with an example of each.**

| Class of nutrients | Nutrients | Example of a food source |
|---|---|---|
| Energy-giving | Carbohydrates | Rice, yam, cassava, bread, sugar |
| Energy-giving (and insulating) | Fats and oils | Palm oil, groundnut oil, butter |
| Body-building (growth and repair) | Proteins | Meat, fish, eggs, beans |
| Protective and regulating | Vitamins | Oranges and pawpaw (vitamin C), carrots (vitamin A) |
| Protective and regulating | Mineral salts | Milk (calcium), liver (iron), iodised salt (iodine) |
| Regulating | Water | Drinking water, fruits |

(Dietary fibre or roughage, found in whole cereals, vegetables and fruits, is also needed in the diet.)
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Differentiate between kwashiorkor and marasmus.

(2 marks)

(ii) State four (4) uses of a food composition table.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Kwashiorkor and marasmus (1 mark each).**

| Kwashiorkor | Marasmus |
|---|---|
| Caused mainly by a **lack of protein** in the diet (the child may still eat some starchy food). It is typical in a child of about one to three years after weaning. The child has **oedema** (a swollen face, belly and feet), thin limbs and pale, thin hair. | Caused by a **lack of food in general, especially energy (a shortage of both energy and protein)**. It is typical in babies under one year (early weaning, bottle-feeding with diluted milk). The child is very thin, with **severe wasting of muscle and fat**, a wrinkled "old man" face, and **no oedema**. |

**(ii) Four uses of a food composition table (1 mark each).**

1. To find the **amount of nutrients and the energy value** in a given mass of a food.
2. To **compare the nutritive value** of different foods and to choose the foods that are richest in a nutrient (for example iron).
3. To **plan balanced meals and diets** that meet the needs of the family and of special groups (children, the sick, pregnant women).
4. To **calculate the nutrients and energy supplied by a recipe or by a day's meals** and to compare them with the daily needs.

questions.enonce_markdown:
List four (4) factors that can influence food availability.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four factors that influence food availability (1 mark each):

1. **Climate and season** (rainfall, drought, flooding): some foods are available only at certain times of the year.
2. **Soil and farming methods**: fertile soil and modern methods give a bigger harvest than poor soil and simple tools.
3. **Transport, storage and marketing facilities**: good roads, markets, and the means of preserving food bring food from the producing areas to the towns and reduce waste.
4. **Income and prices (purchasing power)**: food may be on sale but families with low incomes cannot afford it.

(Other correct points: government policy on imports and exports, pests and diseases, wars, and the size of the population.)
